Codex review: needs changes before merge. ## What this changes This PR standardizes tool-activity typography, spacing, disclosure visibility, and icon sizing. **Example:** A completed edit to agent.ts shows +1 −1 and expandable diff output. - **Before:** The row has larger artwork, looser spacing, and a persistent disclosure arrow. - **After:** The row uses compact typography and calibrated artwork while retaining its file link and expanded diff. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Useful visual evidence and the previous repairs improve confidence, but the remaining label-clipping regression blocks a correctness pass. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** ✨ media proof bonus | Sufficient (screenshot): Inspected before/after screenshots exercise the changed CSS and icon presentation in native Control UI components with synthetic data, showing linked edits, expanded output, tool states, activity masks, and branded images; this establishes the visible component changes rather than full shipped-route execution. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Preference · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Dense tool activity has uneven typography, spacing, and icon emphasis that make transcripts harder to scan. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored direction is an owner decision, and the inspected screenshots demonstrate a coherent improvement using existing presentation owners. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Needs changes before merge - 1 item remains** Keep open: this maintainer-authored visual improvement addresses both prior findings, but one shared-label regression still needs repair. **Priority:** P3 **Reviewed head:** `d08542d05997ba53f7d1e0b1fdc8fc78805f061c` ## Before merge - [ ] **Preserve short identity labels beside long summaries (P2)** - In a 220px standalone ToolMessageSummary, a short label such as “Tool output” shares a flex container with a long output preview. Changing the label from flex: none to a shrinkable auto basis with min-width: 0 distributes compression across both elements, clipping the identity label even though the description could yield instead. This restores the failure addressed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/139372. Keep short identity labels non-shrinking and apply long-name truncation without sacrificing them; cover the narrow label-plus-preview case in the existing browser suite. This rule was unchanged in the previously reviewed head, and I missed it in that earlier review. ## Findings - [P2] Preserve short identity labels beside long summaries — `ui/src/styles/chat/tool-cards.css:302-305` ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: The supplied component previews do not demonstrate short-label preservation beside a long preview in a narrow shipped Chat view.
Agent review details ### How this fits together The Control UI renders tool calls, results, and plugin artwork as transcript rows with expandable details; these changes affect their browser presentation. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Tool calls and results] --> B[Existing display model] B --> C[Solid tool rows] D[Plugin activity artwork] --> C C --> E[Shared chat styles] E --> F[Transcript and expanded details] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep the presentation changes while preserving short identity labels and truncating adjacent descriptions through the existing shared CSS owner. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Source establishes the remaining clipping path: a narrow standalone summary places its short identity label beside a long description, and both now shrink; no target code was executed. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The existing CSS and icon owners are appropriate, and the change needs no additional architecture; the shared label rule should preserve the earlier readability contract. Full review comments: - [P2] Preserve short identity labels beside long summaries — `ui/src/styles/chat/tool-cards.css:302-305` In a 220px standalone ToolMessageSummary, a short label such as “Tool output” shares a flex container with a long output preview. Changing the label from flex: none to a shrinkable auto basis with min-width: 0 distributes compression across both elements, clipping the identity label even though the description could yield instead. This restores the failure addressed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/139372. Keep short identity labels non-shrinking and apply long-name truncation without sacrificing them; cover the narrow label-plus-preview case in the existing browser suite. This rule was unchanged in the previously reviewed head, and I missed it in that earlier review. Confidence: 0.94 Late finding: first raised on code an earlier review cycle already covered. Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.94 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant.
